# routeros_routing_filter_community_ext_list (Resource)


## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "routeros_routing_filter_community_ext_list" "list" {
  list     = "example"
  comment  = "Managed by OpenTofu"
  disabled = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `list` (String) Name of the extended community list this entry belongs to. All the entries sharing the same name form a single list that can be referenced from the routing filter rules.

### Optional

- `___id___` (Number) <em>Resource ID type (.id / name). This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___path___` (String) <em>Resource path for CRUD operations. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `___skip___` (String) <em>A set of transformations for field names. This is an internal service field, setting a value is not required.</em>
- `comment` (String)
- `communities` (Set of String) A set of extended communities that belong to this list. Every element carries the type prefix followed by the value, the supported types are `rt` (Route Target) and `soo` (Site of Origin), for example `rt:1.1.1.1:222`.
- `disabled` (Boolean)
- `place_before` (String) Before which position the rule will be inserted.  
	> Please check the effect of this option, as it does not work as you think!  
	> Best way to use in conjunction with a data source. See [example](../data-sources/ip_firewall.md#example-usage).
- `regexp` (String) A regular expression that is matched against the extended community values instead of the exact `communities` set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.

## Import
Import is supported using the following syntax:
```shell
#The ID can be found via API or the terminal
#The command for the terminal is -> :put [/routing/filter/community-ext-list get [print show-ids]]
terraform import routeros_routing_filter_community_ext_list.list "*1"
```
